claims.text: Nanoscale compositional segregation occurs or can be induced in HfNbTaTiZr.
Segregated regions in HfNbTaTiZr have thermal expansion coefficients distinct from those of the surrounding matrix.
Thermal expansion mismatch between segregated regions and the matrix creates internal residual stresses.
The mismatch-induced residual stresses modify dislocation mobility.
The mismatch-induced residual stresses modify the effective elastic stiffness of the lattice.
Segregation-induced residual stresses govern both stress–strain response and thermoelastic behavior over a wide temperature range.
Rapid quenching can produce a comparatively homogeneous HfNbTaTiZr microstructure with minimal nanoscale segregation.
Prolonged annealing at 600–800 °C promotes nanoscale compositional segregation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealed, segregated specimens will exhibit greater local lattice-parameter variation than rapidly quenched specimens.
Local lattice-parameter variation will indicate differential thermal expansion.
Annealed, segregated specimens will have greater residual internal stress than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Annealed, segregated specimens will show altered dislocation dynamics relative to the rapidly quenched baseline.
Annealed, segregated specimens will have lower tensile creep rates at 1250 °C than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Annealed, segregated specimens will show a distinct, potentially nonlinear, elastic-modulus dependence on temperature from 293 to 1100 K.
A rapidly quenched homogeneous baseline has more uniform thermal expansion and standard dislocation dynamics.
The proposed behavior spans temperatures from 293 K to 1250 °C and deformation modes ranging from cold rolling to tensile creep.
Grain-boundary effects and short-range order may also contribute to the measured behavior.
